extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians (prospective authors, referees, and editors interested in the new journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and acceptance criteria for Discrete Analysis, an arXiv-overlay mathematics journal: scope, submission/licensing requirements, peer-review practices, editorial conflict management, costs, and how accepted papers will be presented and cited. Intended to guide potential authors and contributors about what the journal expects and how it will operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope is a 'cluster of related subjects' (a 'family resemblance') centred on additive combinatorics but including harmonic analysis, ergodic theory, topological dynamics, growth in groups, analytic number theory, combinatorial number theory, extremal combinatorics, probabilistic combinatorics, combinatorial geometry, convexity, metric geometry, and the more mathematical side of theoretical computer science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal does not want to be a fully general mathematics journal but aims to be broad; if in doubt about suitability, consult an editor. The editors will try to err on the side of inclusiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication charges (diamond open access)
rubrics_metrics.description: No charges for readers and no charges for authors — the journal is a 'diamond open access journal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers are hosted on the arXiv so there are no reader charges; initial operating funds cover submission handling costs, and the hope is that charges will not be necessary. Worst-case scenario: a very small submission fee ("roughly equal to the cost of a couple of beers") might be asked in the future, but this is unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission handling software cost and funding model
rubrics_metrics.description: The refereeing-management software is provided by Scholastica at a cost of $10 per submission; Cambridge University provided a grant to cover the first ~500 submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives such as the Episciences platform (free) or Open Journal Systems (requires technical skill) were considered; the $10 fee is compared to much higher article processing charges at conventional journals. In cases of immediately obvious rejections, Scholastica will not charge if notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission workflow (arXiv-first requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should first post their paper on the arXiv and then submit by providing an arXiv link via the journal's submission page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When posting to arXiv, authors should select one of the CC-BY options for the version intended to be the journal's final version; if the paper's license was different originally, authors can re-license the revised (final) version as CC-BY. To submit, go to the journal site and click the 'Submit Manuscript' button and follow the instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing for funder compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are asked to select one of the CC-BY options on arXiv when posting the paper to ensure compliance with open-access requirements of various funding bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper was originally posted under a more restrictive licence, authors can choose a CC-BY licence for the revised final version. Community discussion noted funder concerns about non-commercial or share-alike licences (e.g. CC-BY-NC-SA may be unacceptable for some funders) and recommended CC-BY(-SA) where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review model (traditional refereeing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal will use traditional peer review: editors will find referees, gathering quick opinions and more detailed reports, to decide which arXiv preprints are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions will be made in the usual refereeing way; reviews will be solicited in both concise and detailed forms. The editors also plan to provide short neutral descriptions of accepted papers (based on abstract/introduction and editorial/referee context) rather than publishing critical assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for acceptance — 'genuinely interesting' work
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal aims to 'publish genuinely interesting papers' in the stated areas and to be 'consistently interesting' without setting standards so high that nothing is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intentionally imprecise; authors who believe they have proved results likely to interest the editors are encouraged to submit. The editorial board will exercise discretion to balance selectivity with inclusiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision-making and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about journal policy and about accepting or rejecting papers will be made democratically by the whole editorial board; the managing editor has ultimate responsibility for the smooth running but not unilateral authority on policy/acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The managing editor will do somewhat more work than other editors but major policy and acceptance choices are collective. Example given: discussion and vote were used for the journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors as authors (conflict management and higher standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are allowed to submit papers to the journal, but submissions from editors will be subject to slightly more rigorous standards; in borderline cases a paper will be at a disadvantage if an author is an editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will be completely excluded from the discussion of any paper that might lead to a conflict of interest; Scholastica's software supports exclusion of editors from handling particular submissions. The managing editor intends probably to avoid submitting to the journal to avoid conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version of record and linking to arXiv versions
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be an official 'version of record' for each accepted paper (not necessarily the first arXiv version); the journal will provide a link to the official version and also to newer updated arXiv versions if authors update after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The version of record remains fixed to avoid citation problems; when updated versions exist, the journal page will include two links (official version and updated version) plus a brief summary of what changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation/recognition infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles will be treated like journal articles: they will be exclusive to Discrete Analysis, have DOIs, a numbering system, and the journal will have an ISSN; the editors will adhere to MathSciNet's Policy on Indexing Electronic Journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are intended so that articles are recognised as 'real' publications and indexed/listed in MathSciNet and Zentralblatt (the editors are checking indexing status). The numbering/DOI will help with standard citation practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent availability and disaster recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are hosted on arXiv (which mirrors to HAL), and Scholastica performs regular backups; if arXiv were to fold the editors would download accepted and under-review articles and host them elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because arXiv is widely used and mirrored, the editors consider the content secure; Scholastica backups provide recoverability for journal metadata even if its main site fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and discoverability (short descriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each paper the journal will provide not just an arXiv link but also a short description based on the abstract/introduction and any further context editors or referees can give.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These descriptions aim to make the journal browsable and useful without repeatedly clicking to arXiv; they will help readers understand content and allow the journal homepage to be a worthwhile experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude to novel peer-review experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors are cautious about open peer review and post-publication reviews and will start conventionally to maximise success, but remain open to experimenting later and will allow authors to opt out of such experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although editors hold varying views, the initial approach is conservative; the journal will consider new methods in future but will ensure authors can decline participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of obviously unsuitable or malicious bulk submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If somebody submits an obviously unsuitable paper (or many computer-generated papers) the editors can tell Scholastica and will not be charged the $10 for such immediate rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholastica confirmed that in cases of instantly rejected obviously unsuitable material the journal can avoid the $10 fee by notifying them.
